Subject: SOW v3 — questions on liability and warranty

Markus / Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We reviewed the SOW and the legal team flagged a few items that will block procurement unless we get executive sign-off on a couple of points: 

- Ellis requests removal of the broad warranty carveout for downstream use and wants warranty of service uptime to be 99.5% with a 90-day remedy window.
- They are asking for no liability cap for breaches related to data exfiltration and want indemnity to include customer claims arising from misuse.
- Procurement is also pushing for a two-quarter credit on committed spend if we accept their requested changes (they've suggested a 25% concession).

Attached is the SOW they returned (Ellis_SOW_v3.pdf). Can you confirm what is negotiable from Redwood's side and whether this needs exec review? Procurement will not proceed without an explicit exec carveout on liability/indemnity.

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement is working to close this quarter.

—Hannah
Ellis Technologies | Senior Procurement Manager

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SOW v3 — need exec sign-off on liability/warranty carveouts

Folks — forwarding Ellis' returned SOW. Key asks summarized below and my recommended path. See attached redline summary (redline_summary.xlsx).

Summary of Ellis asks:
- Remove liability cap for data exfiltration and broaden indemnity to include customer misuse claims.
- Warranty: 99.5% uptime commitment and 90-day remedy window (they want contractual remedy language).
- Commercial: request 25% discount on committed spend if we accept changes.

My recommendation (what we propose to offer to close this quarter):
1) Liability cap: carve out data breach cap only for proven direct damages tied to Redwood negligence limited to $500,000 OR 12 months of Ellis committed fees (whichever is lower) — explicit carveout language to keep behind CFO/CEO approval.
2) Indemnity: keep Redwood's standard IP indemnity; narrow customer-misuse indemnity and require demonstration of misuse and exhaustion of remediation steps before Redwood liability attaches.
3) Warranty: accept a 99.5% SLO as a commercial SLA, but limit contractual warranty remedies to service credits up to a maximum of 3 months proration (no unlimited refund).
4) Commercial trade: offer a capped one-time concession on committed spend of 20% (not 25%) contingent on exec approval of the liability carveout above.

Why this is a reasonable middle ground: preserves our legal risk posture, gives the customer a tangible concession, and avoids an uncapped exposure precedent. If legal (Priyom) and Laura can approve, I will request final sign-off from the CEO/CFO.

Next steps: Priyom, can you confirm redline language that maps to the liability cap proposed? Laura — if you can weigh in on the commercial 20% vs 25% ask, I can take the package to execs.

Thanks —
Markus
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Markus / team —

Thanks for the summary. I reviewed Ellis' redlines and drafted specific language in the attached redline_summary.xlsx — highlighted changes map to the recommended package below. A few clarifications and a slight tweak to protect Redwood's exposure: 

1) Liability cap: Instead of a flat $500k, suggest a cap equal to the lesser of (a) $750,000 or (b) two times the annual committed fees under the SOW. This gives flexibility if Ellis' committed spend is small or large. We should include an explicit carveout for willful misconduct and fraud (no cap) and a data-exfiltration carveout limited to direct damages only.
2) Indemnity: Maintain our IP indemnity language. For customer-misuse claims, require that Ellis pursue remediation first (reasonable cure steps) and provide us prompt notice; Redwood's indemnity obligation should be proportionate. No open-ended indemnity for third-party claims caused solely by the customer's misuse.
3) Warranty and remedies: Accept SLO of 99.5% as a commercial SLA. Limit contractual remedies to service credits capped at 3x monthly fees (not 3 months of proration) and specify an escalation path before credits apply. 

Commercial concession: legal is comfortable if the commercial concession does not exceed 20% one-time credit and is conditioned on the liability cap language above. 

If we agree to this package, it needs executive approval for the liability cap / carveout. Recommend routing to: CFO (for cap exposure) and CEO for final sign-off on precedent.

I will prepare a redline incorporating the exact cap math and carveout phrasing once we have confirmation from sales on final commercial terms.

—Priyom
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redline_summary.xlsx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Markus / Priyom / Marissa —

I reviewed the recommended package and Priyom's tweak. Given the strategic nature of Ellis and the chance to lock them as a multi-year customer, I approve escalation to execs with the following binding conditions: 

1) Liability cap: Approve a final cap equal to the lesser of $600,000 or two times the annual committed fees (this is our executive exception). Must include the stated carveouts for willful misconduct/fraud (no cap) and a narrowly tailored data-exfiltration carveout limited to proven direct damages.
2) Indemnity: Accept the proposed narrowing for customer-misuse with required remediation steps and prompt notice. No acceptance of broad, open-ended indemnity.
3) Warranty & remedies: Approve SLO 99.5% with contractual remedies limited to service credits capped at 3x monthly fees (as Priyom suggested).
4) Commercial: Approve up to a 20% one-time credit on committed spend (not recurring) contingent on DocuSign executed SOW within 7 business days and legal sign-off on the redline.

Markus — with these conditions, proceed to ask CFO and CEO for formal sign-off and share the redline and the HubSpot deal link. Please include the following in the exec packet: short risk note with exposure calculation under the proposed cap, the redline_summary.xlsx, and the negotiated commercial term summary.

I will be available for the exec call if needed.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
